resolutions.researcher_notes: OPEC Annual Statistical Bulletin 2012 (2011 data), table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members' (pp.75-77), lists the Abqaiq/Berri line, Saudi Aramco, as an existing/in-service gas pipeline. Row confirmed via pdftotext: 'Abqaiq/Berri  Saudi Aramco  85  24/36  na  na'. url_verifier returns HTTP 200 but its substring screen cannot read PDF text (documented PDF false-negative); presence of 'Abqaiq/Berri' + '24/36' confirmed directly in the extracted PDF text. Status 'operating' is inferred from inclusion in the ASB current-infrastructure inventory (no explicit status word). Single source (OPEC), so medium; original opec.org URL is dead (403), Wayback snapshot cited.

Abqaiq/Berri appears specifically in the OPEC ASB 2012 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members' table (not the crude-oil or petroleum-product pipeline tables), directly supporting Fuel = Gas. Confirmed via pdftotext. Same OPEC source origin, so medium.

OPEC ASB 2012 gas-pipelines table gives Abqaiq/Berri length = 85 (the ASB reports length in miles; cross-check: Abqaiq/Yanbu = 741 in this table vs ~1200 km known). 85 miles = 136.8 km, which rounds to the GEM value 137 km (GEM stores '137 km / 85 miles'). Consistent. Confirmed via pdftotext.

OPEC ASB 2012 gas-pipelines table lists diameter '24/36' for Abqaiq/Berri, exactly matching GEM Diameter '24, 36' in. Confirmed via pdftotext. (GEM's own diameter citation was ASB 2017 p.136 — same OPEC series; the 2012 edition carries the identical value.)

Endpoints Abqaiq and Berri are both Saudi Aramco facilities in Saudi Arabia's Eastern Province; the pipeline is listed under Saudi Arabia (Saudi Aramco) in the OPEC ASB 2012 Members table, supporting Start/EndCountryOrArea = Saudi Arabia. Confirmed via pdftotext.
OPEC ASB 2012 gas-pipelines table names the operator/owner of the Abqaiq/Berri line as 'Saudi Aramco', matching GEM Owner1 = Saudi Aramco (100%). Confirmed via pdftotext.
